title: Higher Rates and Stock Market Impacts
summary: Persistent rates, intervention capacity and sector differences.
assessment: The report usefully separates operating resilience from stock valuation and recognizes bank asset/liability interactions. The reserve-spending arithmetic confuses a stock change with a flow, the Schwab example understates deposit migration, and the confident AI crowding-out narrative faces contrary institutional evidence.

claims.claim: Refining remains the immediate energy bottleneck.
claims.reason: EIA’s later assessment confirms especially high distillate and jet-fuel margins amid disrupted refining. The article correctly distinguishes transponder-visible trade from unknown shadow traffic; lack of visible traffic is not proof of zero shipments.

evidence.title: Third-quarter crude prices and refinery margins
evidence.finding: Distillate and jet-fuel spreads were highest amid refining disruption in Russia, China and the Middle East.

claims.claim: Higher discount rates challenge expensive equities.
claims.reason: For unchanged expected cash flows, a higher required return lowers present value. The implication is conditional: stronger earnings expectations can offset the discount-rate effect, so this mechanism does not automatically predict every high-multiple stock will fall.

claims.claim: Higher rates can improve bank earnings.
claims.reason: A wider asset-yield/deposit-cost spread can improve net interest income, but deposit repricing, hedges, securities losses and credit quality can offset it. Government-debt exposure is not automatically safe: duration, currency and sovereign-credit risks remain. Broad reassurance needs bank-specific capital and liquidity data.

claims.claim: Schwab survived because deposits were stable.
claims.reason: Schwab avoided failure, but its deposits were not unchanged: average bank deposits in 2023 were $306.5bn versus $424.2bn in 2022, and replacement funding mattered. The distinction is deposit composition, available liquidity and outflow speed, not absence of deposit migration.

evidence.title: Schwab 2023 results
evidence.finding: Average bank deposits fell from $424.168bn in 2022 to $306.505bn in 2023; reported funding costs increased.

claims.claim: Hyperscaler borrowing crowds out other sectors.
claims.reason: Large AI borrowing creates a plausible competition channel, but the Treasury advisory committee later found no clear evidence of crowding out Treasuries or non-tech credit and emphasized growth-driven real yields. This is competing evidence, not proof the effect is zero; issuance volume alone does not identify causal rate pressure.

claims.claim: Geographic diversification can reduce volatility.
claims.reason: With imperfectly correlated holdings, diversification can reduce variance relative to concentrated exposure at comparable weights. The benefit is conditional and can shrink during common shocks; geographic labels alone do not ensure different economic risks.

proof.derivation: Portfolio variance includes covariance terms; correlations below one reduce variance relative to a perfectly correlated combination of the same component volatilities.

coverage_note: Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.
framework_lessons: A stock change is not the transaction flow that caused it.
Bank risk depends on funding, asset duration and liquidity together.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
